idiom_name: tagged union: enum discriminant + union payload + switch
implementation_notes: C has neither sealing nor an exhaustiveness check, so the classic Visitor structure disappears but so does the proof: model the closed set explicitly as a struct carrying an enum kind tag plus a union of per-variant payload structs, give each kind a constructor function that sets the tag and initialises exactly one union member, and write one switch (s->kind) per operation. Coverage is only warning-level - GCC/Clang -Wswitch warns when an enum-typed switch omits a named enumerator and has no default, and -Wswitch-enum keeps warning even in the presence of a default - so build with warnings-as-errors and keep a default: abort() arm as the run-time backstop. Keep this hand-written structure for tag-and-union APIs (wire formats, embedded code); where the set is open or behaviour dominates, prefer an opaque struct with a function-pointer table, which is the C equivalent of the polymorphism the pattern retires elsewhere.
pitfalls: Nothing enforces closure: any translation unit can invent a new tag value or cast an arbitrary int into the enum, so 'exhaustive' only means 'complete as long as the build is warning-clean'.
Reading the wrong union member is undefined behaviour rather than a cast error - tag and payload must be updated together, by convention only.
A default arm silences -Wswitch, and -Wswitch-enum is noisy on enums used as bitmasks, so the check has to be curated per switch and is easy to lose in a refactor.
